tagline: Through the national forest to the only city in the county.
intro: KY 89 starts at its junction with KY 490 in Rockcastle County and runs thirty-five miles northeast into Jackson County, through McKee and on to the Estill County line. A quarter of Jackson County lies in the Daniel Boone National Forest. The county sits on the edge of the Cumberland Plateau, and its motto calls it the place where the mountains and the bluegrass blend.
McKee is the county seat and its only city. In 2019 it voted to allow the sale of alcohol, which left the city wet and the county moist.

moments.title: Cruise
moments.text: A crossroads named for an early settler and entrepreneur called Cruise, which got its post office in 1899.

moments.title: McKee
moments.text: The town lies in the valley of Pigeon Roost Creek and keeps the centermost trailhead of the Sheltowee Trace, which takes its name from Big Turtle, the Shawnee name for Daniel Boone.

moments.title: Arthur Lakes Log House
moments.text: Up Lakes Creek Road, a two-room saddlebag house from about 1890, built of oak logs at the bottom, tulip poplar in the middle and pine at the top.

sources.label: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet, Kentucky State and National Scenic Byways and Highways
